snippet.title: How to reverse engineer PandaDoc with Claude: what passed, what broke
snippet.description:
Claude built a PandaDoc alternative from one Markdown spec: all 29 acceptance checks passed in a real browser, along with 47 automated tests.
The test build also exposed 8 gaps in the spec, and every one is now fixed.

We gave Claude one Markdown spec for a small-team quote builder and had it build the tool in four phases: the foundation with clients, the price list and settings; quotes and pricing; approval, sending and the client page; and expiry, printing and invoices. The core rule: a quote whose total discount is over the 15% threshold needs a manager's approval before it can be sent, and no manager can approve their own quote. The gaps included sign-in that matched people by email when the seed people had no emails, a Duplicate action that didn't say what gets copied, and an approval request with no other manager to approve it. What passed, what broke, what we didn't test, and when PandaDoc is still worth paying for.
